elbow_flex.source: ACE Bicep Curl (the ACE page shows the barbell version, "wrists, elbows and shoulders in a straight line" at the start, i.e. near-extended; the elbow-position and torso cues generalize to the dumbbell curl, illustrative 5-degree start): "Lift the barbell toward the shoulders while bending the elbows." PMC6047503 (EMG of curl variants) measured the dumbbell curl's excursion at 123.1 +/- 12.3 degrees, so the end is the 5-degree start plus that excursion, about 128 degrees

shoulder_flex.source: ACE Bicep Curl (barbell page, cue generalized): "keeping them next to the middle of the body"; ACE Seated Biceps Curl (dumbbell): "without arching your back or moving your elbows forward"

torso_lean.source: ACE Bicep Curl (barbell page, cue generalized): "Keep chest still, using just the arms for the movement"

muscles.peakSource: PMC6047503 (EMG of curl variants): "the eccentric phase showed lower EMG activity with respect to the concentric phase for both muscles investigated," so biceps effort is highest through the lift, easing on the way down

mistake.name: Swing and drift

tells.text: The torso rocks back to sling the weight up.
The elbows swing forward off the ribs.

mistake.source: BuiltWithScience biomechanics test (Coach Kassem): "allowing the elbows to excessively sway forward during bicep curls led to less biceps activation and more front delts activation"; ACE Bicep Curl (barbell page, cue generalized): "Keep chest still, using just the arms"

sources: Contact fact (D-FG7 (j), both arms together): ACE Seated Biceps Curl describes a "closed, supinated grip (palms facing forward)" held for the dumbbell curl; no wrist_pron range is kept, since the side view does not draw that channel (D-FG7 (l))
